equivalence_note: AST equality is not effect equality. Equal ASTs exclude comments/formatting but say nothing about imported modules, files read at run time, environment or interpreter behaviour; unequal ASTs are classified only by the stated static rules. Table effects are a static replay of module-level literals, not an execution.

added_profiles_to_existing_pairs.note: Windows-only only because the first profile for this pair has row-0 mode None (row order); an earlier non-None profile for the same pair would admit it on Linux and the mode-None rows would then accept any mode

admission.model: Model, checked against the function source: profiles matching helper_pair = (row0 sha256, row1 sha256) are selected in table order; `windows = profiles[0][0][3] is None`, and windows refuses unless os.name == 'nt'. So a pair is Linux-admitted iff the FIRST profile with that pair has a non-None row-0 mode.
